gen-gf-comic-relief-mulish: Blunt, bold strokes with open-ended bowls: that's Comic Relief. Mulish takes over below with a sans-serif build, horseshoe-open apertures and a large x-height, so the heading's loudness lands on something friendly and easygoing.
gen-gf-comic-relief-poppins: Bowls left unfinished on one side give Comic Relief its swagger. Poppins sits below as a sans with tall, sturdy lowercase and loose curves, taking the shout down a notch without any thick-thin flicker.
gen-gf-comic-relief-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab sets a slab-serif texture where the middle zone dominates the line. Comic Relief's bold, unfinished bowls bring the play, while the slab's structure and open throats bring order.
gen-gf-comme-fs-erode: Erode brings a serif with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. Comme heads it in sans-serif, tight and contemporary, its c opened like calipers, a tidy foil for all that dignity.
gen-gf-comme-fs-karma: Comme is a sans-serif with tight vertical rhythm and little ascender. Where Comme keeps things compact, Karma, a text serif, lets terminals finish well away from the stem with a modulation that never snags the eye.
gen-gf-cossette-texte-fs-erode: Erode is a serif with a tall middle band and shallow ascenders. As the text runs on, Erode's broad openings and gentle weight shifts keep it moving, while Cossette Texte's plain single-weight lines hold back.
gen-gf-cossette-texte-fs-karma: Karma, a text serif, tapers its joins modestly without ever letting them vanish. But Cossette Texte draws wirelike strokes of one thickness, so the heading stays plain while the body supplies the shading.
gen-gf-cossette-titre-fs-karma: Letters huddle like pencils bundled in a tin in Cossette Titre, a sans-serif with open-faced curves and a tall middle band. Karma's sturdy thin lines give the pair its trustworthy footing.
gen-gf-courier-prime-fs-merriweather-san: Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, its e opening clearly to the right. And over paragraph after paragraph, those sturdy words keep the eye moving, with Courier Prime's measured fixed-width beat reserved for the heading.
gen-gf-courier-prime-fs-supreme: Courier Prime lays down fixed-width, code-style letters with a measured, spaced-out beat and no calligraphic thinning. Supreme, a sans, brings the heft instead: a thick, crisp strip of text with letters held open, not curled shut.
